cf.title: Unify parallel worker handling for index builds

input.subject: Unify parallel worker handling for index builds and instrumentation

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only objection raised, maintenance-fit-1, was refuted because Postgres does not keep its C API stable across major versions. The series fixes two reported bugs and removes duplicated code, with support in messages #2 and #3. Confidence is low because nobody has reviewed v2, and the wrong-results claim has no reproducing test in the material.

brief.title: Shared helpers for parallel index builds, with GIN and BRIN fixes
brief.problem: nbtree, GIN and BRIN each carry near-identical code for parallel worker setup, shared memory and leader-worker communication, and parallel vacuum duplicates the query text handling. This duplication has hidden bugs: GIN workers report query ID 0, and parallel BRIN and GIN builds never set indcheckxmin after a broken HOT chain, so older snapshots can use the index and get wrong results.
brief.proposed_design: Two bug fixes come first: GIN workers report the leader's query ID, and BRIN and GIN pass the broken HOT chain flag back to the leader, backpatched to 17 and 18. Then a new parallel_index_build module gives AMs shared helpers for context creation, shared memory, worker wait, abort and end, and a common ParallelIndexBuildScan() records broken HOT chains itself. Separate helpers in parallel.c handle query text for index builds and vacuum.
user_visible_surface: New C API header access/parallel_index_build.h with ParallelIndexBuildCreateContext (takes library_name), ParallelIndexBuildReportScanDone, ParallelIndexBuildWaitForWorkers, ParallelIndexBuildAbort, ParallelIndexBuildEnd.
New C API ParallelIndexBuildScan() that joins the shared scan, runs table_index_build_scan() and records broken HOT chains.
New query text helpers in access/parallel.h, including RestoreParallelQueryText(), for parallel workers.
pg_stat_activity shows the leader's query_id for parallel GIN build workers instead of 0.
Parallel BRIN and GIN builds now set indcheckxmin when they meet a broken HOT chain.
author_claims: Parallel BRIN and GIN builds fail to set indcheckxmin, so a transaction with an older snapshot can get wrong results.
The HOT chain fix should be backpatched to 17 for BRIN and 18 for GIN.
ParallelIndexBuildEnd now requires workers to report WAL and buffer usage, which the author finds acceptable for extensions.
A sketched pgvector port shows a net code reduction, plus a shim of about 330 lines for older versions.
pgvector has the same query ID and broken HOT chain bugs, and the new helpers fix them.
brief.thread_state: Sami Imseih and Michael Paquier supported the query text and index build helpers; Michael objected to the larger Instrumentation struct in shared memory, so v1 0001 and 0002 were dropped. v2 adds two bug fixes and ParallelIndexBuildScan(), and nobody has reviewed v2 yet.
unclear: The material does not show a test that reproduces the wrong results from the missing indcheckxmin in BRIN or GIN.
The patches do not say which fixes go to back branches and whether those differ from the master versions.
The thread does not say whether the shared mutex will let AMs add their own fields, such as pgvector's inertia field.
The material does not say how out-of-core AMs learn of the new ParallelIndexBuildEnd requirement for WAL and buffer usage.
The material reports no performance or shared memory measurements for v2.

refuted.title: New extension-facing build API may need to change again soon
refuted.failure_scenario: pgvector and other out-of-core AMs move to ParallelIndexBuildCreateContext and ParallelIndexBuildEnd, carrying a shim of about 330 lines. Then the stack-based instrumentation work changes how worker WAL and buffer usage is passed, or an AM needs its own fields under the shared mutex. The API changes again, and each extension carries a second shim.
refuted.argument: Patch 0003 takes library_name so that extensions can use these helpers, which makes them extension API. Message #7 says the fields under the ParallelIndexBuildShared mutex are fixed, so pgvector needs a second spinlock and nbtree keeps havedead in shared state. ParallelIndexBuildEnd now requires WAL and buffer usage reporting, while messages #5 and #6 deferred the instrumentation design until stack-based instrumentation is settled. A committer would likely ask whether the API should be frozen before that design is known.
refuted.author_must_show: How would the shared state and ParallelIndexBuildEnd hold AM-specific fields and a changed instrumentation design without breaking extensions that adopt them in this release?

critic.reasoning: Postgres does not keep its C API stable across major versions, and extensions that opt in to these helpers already carry per-version shims, so a later API change is routine cost. Message #7 shows the helpers fit three in-core AMs and a pgvector port.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: Patch 0002 makes parallel BRIN and GIN builds set the existing pg_index.indcheckxmin flag; no catalog definition changes.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: New header access/parallel_index_build.h and query text helpers in access/parallel.h are usable by out-of-core index AMs.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: With indcheckxmin set, transactions with older snapshots no longer use a newly built BRIN or GIN index.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Patch 0002 proposes a backpatch to 17 for BRIN and 18 for GIN.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new shared module in access/common becomes the path for parallel builds in nbtree, GIN and BRIN.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is there a test or script that reproduces wrong results from a parallel BRIN or GIN build that met a broken HOT chain?
Which patches go to the back branches, and do the 17 and 18 versions of 0002 differ from the master version?
Is the GIN query ID fix in 0001 also meant for backpatch to 18?
How does an out-of-core AM learn that ParallelIndexBuildEnd now requires workers to report WAL and buffer usage?
Can an AM keep its own fields under the shared mutex, or must it add a second lock as the pgvector sketch does?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier supported the query text and index build helpers in message #3, but only for v1. The backpatched fix in 0002 needs someone who knows index builds, HOT chains and indcheckxmin.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a correctness fix on stable branches 17 and 18, and for a shared module that every parallel index build in nbtree, GIN and BRIN runs through from now on.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 after review, dropped the two patches Michael Paquier objected to, and moved the CommitFest entry forward on 2026-10-31.

priority.reason: Patch 0002 fixes a reported wrong-results case in parallel BRIN and GIN builds, and the refactoring removes duplicated code without new user-facing surface. Review cost is medium because 0003 and 0005 are large and touch three index AMs; 0001 and 0002 are small and can go first.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the wrong-results claim, the safety of the 0002 backpatch for extension ABI, and the behaviour of ParallelIndexBuildScan() in 0005 are unchecked. Nobody has reviewed v2 yet.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: speeding up GIN build with parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch splits a GIN index build between parallel workers, each scanning a range of heap blocks and building its own rbtree of entries. The workers send sorted entries through shared memory to the leader, which merges them and writes each key once; the leader later also takes part as a worker.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In April Robert Haas moved it to the next CommitFest because it had too little review and too few comments. He also found no parallel-safety check for expression indexes, workers opening the heap and index with no lock, and no agreement on the gin_shared_mem GUCs. Michael Paquier returned it with feedback mainly because of Heikki Linnakangas's suggestion to keep the rbtree but flush it to tapes and merge them with the tuplesort.c machinery from Peter Geoghegan's parallel B-tree patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we flushed the tree to a tape instead, then we could perhaps use the machinery that Peter's parallel B-tree patch is adding to tuplesort.c, to merge the tapes.

precedents_retrieved.title: create index failed. PARALLEL UNSAFE function does not prevent parallel index build
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made plan_create_index_workers() check parallel safety on the raw index expressions and predicate, read from the pg_index syscache, so that a PARALLEL UNSAFE function folded to a constant still prevents a parallel index build. The bug report showed CREATE INDEX failing in a parallel worker because a plpgsql function with an EXCEPTION block was const-folded before the check.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed and then reverted after Tom Lane objected. He said it does not fix the failure, which returns when the function is marked PARALLEL SAFE, and that it breaks the planner rule that original markings stop mattering once a function is inlined or const-folded. He also said that passing raw parse-analysis output to is_parallel_safe() misses parallel-unsafe default arguments, and he preferred making exception-using functions parallel safe through a separate commitfest patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's a band-aid
that doesn't really solve the problem: if I simply declare the
function as PARALLEL SAFE, the failure comes right back.

precedents_retrieved.title: improve DEBUG1 logging of parallel workers for CREATE INDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the DEBUG1 message for parallel CREATE INDEX to report parallel workers launched as well as planned. It later grew into a CREATE INDEX (VERBOSE) option, with matching REINDEX (VERBOSE) output, that reports parallel worker use at INFO level.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it after Michael Paquier pointed to Tom's view that such details should come from an extended EXPLAIN rather than VERBOSE options on more commands. Michael also asked how clients would consume the output. The author wrote that the best approach needs more discussion, and that fixing only the REINDEX DEBUG1 output did not make much sense.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm +-0 about the
VERBOSE option attached to more commands, as it is a bit harder for
clients to catch the information wanted.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel CREATE INDEX for GiST indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel CREATE INDEX for GiST, limited to unsorted builds without buffering, with workers inserting tuples into a shared index. Page splits are detected through fake LSNs from GetFakeLSNForUnloggedRel(), and the pages are WAL-logged at the end.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer objected to the code: Andrey Borodin found it correct and suggested only a refactor of the LSN choice. In the last message the author said he was worried that GiST would have too many build methods, because a parallel build can use much more CPU without being faster. He said parallel buffered builds might settle this, but he had no time to study them and someone else would have to. The visible messages show no further work and no closing message.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But for parallel builds it's not that clear - it can easily happen that we use much more CPU, without speeding anything up.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow setting parallel_workers on partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow the parallel_workers reloption on partitioned tables, so that the planner uses it to choose the number of workers for a Parallel Append over the partitions. A later version also let grouping relations take the setting from the partitioned table they read, for partitionwise aggregation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley questioned the semantics: a high setting on the partitioned table can request more workers than the partitions use, and the number does not shrink when the planner or run-time pruning removes partitions. Laurenz Albe and Amit Langote agreed the design needed more thought, and Amit Langote suggested a separate parallel_append_workers option. The thread then stalled, the patch stopped applying, and Daniel Gustafsson marked it Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If someone sets the partitioned table's parallel_workers high so that
they get a large number of workers when no partitions are pruned
during planning, do they really want the same number of workers in
queries where a large number of partitions are pruned?

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallelize correlated subqueries that execute within each worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build parallel plans for queries with correlated subplans when each subplan runs entirely within one parallel worker, so no Param value has to pass between workers. After review, the design changed to treat PARAM_EXEC params as parallel safe by default, track required params on each rel, and insert a Gather node only where that set is empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread shows no author reply after Tomas Vondra's July 2024 review, and the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024. That review found that regression tests failed on a changed plan in select_parallel, reported a compiler warning, and listed code comments. It also said no reviewer was able to confirm that the PARAM handling is correct.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And in general the patch looks reasonably simple and clean, but my knowledge of PARAM intricacies is pretty much nil, so I'm hesitant to claim the patch is correct.

precedents_retrieved.title: system load consideration hook for parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Tom Lane, Peter Geoghegan
precedents_retrieved.summary: Before starting parallel workers, check the current system load and reduce the number of workers when the system is busy, so parallel query does not slow down other sessions at peak load. The author proposed a hook for this and later posted a POC patch that measures CPU load and picks the worker count from the free CPUs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that a load-based control for parallel workers alone is premature before there is field experience with parallel query, and that the problem covers all process types. He also did not trust system load metrics as a gatekeeper, since load averages lag by about a minute, and found the POC code platform-specific and poorly documented. He suggested refining the existing process-count settings instead, and closed the entry as not favored by the community.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We don't yet have enough field experience with the parallel query
facilities to know what kind of use patterns there are and what systems
for load management we need.  So I think building a highly specific
system like this seems premature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add parallel columns for seq scan and index scan on pg_stat_all_tables and _indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel_seq_scan, last_parallel_seq_scan, parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan columns to pg_stat_all_tables, and parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan to pg_stat_all_indexes. The goal is to help administrators judge how parallel workers are used and tune parallelism settings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers doubted that per-table and per-index counts of parallel scans help with tuning, since parallel plans with Gather nodes are usually analyzed per statement. Michael Paquier added that the metrics committed in e7a9496de906 and 5d4298e75f25 may already cover the need. Robert Haas found no clear use case for these counters. The author agreed that the committed metrics were good enough for now.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the question to which we don't have a clear answer is: for what purpose would you want to be able to distinguish parallel and non-parallel scans on a per-table basis?

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the retrieved list has no earlier attempt at shared parallel index build helpers or at the GIN and BRIN fixes. The thread also points to no earlier discussion of this idea, so no prior rejection reason can be applied.

The series adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog column, psql feature or dump-relevant object, so the user-facing contract barely moves. The visible changes are bug fixes: GIN workers now show the leader's query_id, and BRIN and GIN builds now set indcheckxmin as nbtree already does. After a minor upgrade, some older-snapshot transactions may skip a newly built index, which is the documented and correct behaviour. Extension API questions belong to another angle.

The series adds no on-disk, WAL, wire protocol or catalog change. The 0002 fix only sets the existing pg_index.indcheckxmin flag, and that flag reaches standbys through normal catalog WAL. Leader-to-worker state lives in per-build DSM between processes of one server binary, so mixed versions cannot meet. The structs 0002 changes for 17 and 18 appear to be private to brin.c and gininsert.c, so the backpatch should not break extension ABI; this needs checking against the code. Indexes built in parallel before the fix need no repair, because indcheckxmin only protects snapshots older than the build. The new C API exists only on master. The nbtree VACUUM invariant does not apply, because the patch changes index build code, not VACUUM.

The proposal adds no new privilege or exposure surface: query text and query_id reach pg_stat_activity under existing visibility rules, and library_name follows CreateParallelContext. The indcheckxmin fix concerns correctness of results, not access control, and no new memory use falls under user control.

The nbtree VACUUM invariant does not apply because this proposal changes index builds only. Committer Michael Paquier supported the index build and query text helpers in message #3, but nobody has reviewed v2 or 0005 yet.

Postgres has no shared parallel index build helper today. The patches build on CreateParallelContext, shm_toc and table_index_build_scan() and do not replace them, so they add no second mechanism. The BRIN and GIN fixes cover bugs that no current feature or extension handles.

Demand holds up. The bug fixes address wrong query results and a wrong query_id, and the refactoring has support from a committer (message #3) and another reviewer (message #2). It also has a sketched port by one out-of-core index AM, pgvector (message #7), which has the same bugs. Whether the new extension API should be public is a design question for other angles.
